summary: Computer-use tool for AI agents that reads and operates desktop apps on macOS, Windows and Linux through the accessibility tree, without screenshots.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: agent-desktop gives AI agents computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads a desktop app's accessibility tree and returns it as JSON with a ref for every element, so an agent can click, type and verify by ref. It works as a CLI, an MCP server over stdio or a C library, and ships agent guides inside the binary.
sixtySeconds.problem: Screenshot-based computer use is slow and error-prone. Using the OS accessibility tree gives agents precise, structured control of desktop apps.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for structured JSON output, refs instead of coordinates, MCP support and the same tool on all three major desktop OSes.
requirements: macOS 13+, Windows 10 1809+, or Ubuntu 24.04+ (X11 or Wayland)
Node.js for the npm install, or Homebrew, or a native release archive

overview: Install with npm (or Bun, Yarn, pnpm, or Homebrew on macOS/Linux), then run agent-desktop status to see platform and permissions. On macOS, agent-desktop permissions --guide walks you through granting Accessibility access.
Take a snapshot of an app's interactive elements, act on a ref, then snapshot again to verify. agent-desktop mcp serves every command as an MCP tool.
Snapshots, clipboard reads and screenshots can contain private desktop content, so keep them out of public logs. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.

steps.title: Act on a ref
steps.body: Use a ref from the snapshot, e.g. agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8.

steps.body: Take another snapshot to confirm the change.
